How Libertarian Is Rand Paul on Drug Policy?

The elder Paul, who ran for president on the Libertarian Party's ticket in 1988, is more openly and consistently libertarian than his son.

Paul the Younger is his father's son, and grew up seeing his father's battles. It is my belief that he is far more libertarian that he lets on, but knows how to play the game of politics far better than his father ever did. Even if I am wrong, he is a step in the right direction, and a not-perfect-but-still-supportable candidate who actually has a chance to bring our ideals to the national stage.

I love Johnson, but his career shows the futility of trying to get someone with an L after their name on a national ticket; far better to push Libertarian party candidates on state and local tickets, building the groundwork for a nationally viable 3rd party down the road, while working with "the best we can do" candidates from the two major parties.
Exactly. I'm not in love with Rand but I love the idea of turning the Republicans more to the Libertarian side of things. This is the audience they need to appease in order to win the White House.

I think horror to a degree depends on what scares you. (Bear with me I promise I'm not trying to be obnoxious as shit)

Traditional horror:

  • Something classic like Dracula, anything Poe, Lovecraft etc
  • Interview with a Vampire by Ann Rice
  • American Psycho

Personally I've always enjoyed "non-traditional" horror. Stuff like:

  • Blood Meridian by Cormac McCarthy
  • Never Let Me Go by Kazuo Ishiguro
  • Heart of Darkness by Conrad
  • The Handmaid's Tale by Atwood

I would even count things like So We Came To an End by Joshua Ferris, The Pale King by David Foster Wallace, and The Stranger by Camus.
